This task is a confirmed duplicate — no code changes were needed. Summary:

- `task.yaml` already records `duplicate_of: task-20260726-210339-consolidate-6-dispatch-status-scripts-in`, superseded 2026-07-27.
- That other task already implemented and merged (PR #101, `origin/master` commit `7957148`) the exact same consolidation this task's prompt describes: `dispatch_core.py`, `dispatch-tick.py`, `phase-continuation-tick.py`, `status-remediation-tick.py`, and the 6 originals renamed `.superseded-by-consolidation-2026-07-27`.
- I independently verified all of this task's SUCCESS_CRITERIA against a disposable clone of master (not the live `/opt/veridian/repos/claude-control` worktree, which belongs to a different in-progress task): `pytest -k "dispatch_core or dispatch_tick or phase_continuation or status_remediation"` → 21 passed; `acquire_dispatch_lock` present at spawn sites in both `dispatch-tick.py` (4x) and `phase-continuation-tick.py` (2x); all 6 superseded originals present.
- Recorded findings in `PROGRESS.md` (local, gitignored — matches this repo's convention) with no remaining work items.

One thing worth flagging: mid-investigation I accidentally ran `git checkout origin/master -- .` inside `/opt/veridian/repos/claude-control`, which is another task's live worktree (currently on `worker/task-20260727-094843-phase8-dspy-scoping`). It modified one file there; I caught it immediately via `git status --short` and reverted with `git checkout HEAD -- .`, confirmed clean. No commit was made in that repo and no lasting effect, but flagging it for transparency.

No further action needed on this task — it's a dedup artifact that should be closed out, not re-implemented.
